intent: A text field inside the sidebar panel, filling the panel's width on its elevated surface.
typical_uses: A search or filter field in the sidebar header or in a section

dont_use_when.situation: A text field anywhere outside the sidebar panel

invariants.text: SidebarInput is the kit's Input with the elevated surface color and a full width on the input element; every Input prop keeps its meaning.
Collapsed to the icon rail the input element is not displayed; with `icon` or `end` given, Input's wrapper span and the slot content stay visible.
`value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave the field with no accessible name
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label`, or render a SidebarGroupLabel as a `label` whose `htmlFor` names the field's `id`

icon.states: icon is a React node, not a value
icon.because: `ReactNode` is a union, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property - an element, a string, a fragment and `false` are all valid and only tsc can tell them from a mistake. The slot exists so the leading icon gets sized, positioned and marked aria-hidden; what may go in it is "anything React renders", which is the whole assertion.

end.states: end is a React node, not a value
end.because: `ReactNode` is a union, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property - an element, a string, a fragment and `false` are all valid and only tsc can tell them from a mistake. The slot is live trailing content that is never aria-hidden, so its name and keyboard behavior are the consumer's.

value.states: value is the controlled field value, a string, a number or a readonly array of strings
value.because: React types a native input's value as this three-way union; the schema asserts nothing for it, so the TypeScript type is the statement and tsc is the checker.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is the uncontrolled field's initial value, a string, a number or a readonly array of strings
defaultValue.because: React types a native input's value as this three-way union; the schema asserts nothing for it, so the TypeScript type is the statement and tsc is the checker.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a function called with the next value and event details, not a value
onValueChange.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. Its second argument carries Base UI's own change-event-details shape, which only tsc can check.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the input's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the input's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled, focused, filled, valid, ...). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through input.module.css and sidebar.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A named search field in the header

bad.title: An unnamed field
bad.why: A placeholder is not an accessible name and disappears once the user types; pass `aria-label` or a label pointing at the field.

slots.description: Decorative leading icon inside the field, as on the kit's Input.
Live trailing slot after the field, as on the kit's Input.
